title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-02-27
source: Ampex MM-1000 16 Track Master Two Inch Wide Tape; Multi Track Mix-down To DAT By Dan Healy @ 44.1KHz) circa 1995?; DAT x ONE by Dick Latvala- DAT x TWO via either Dick or Rob Bertrando; Editing (Adobe Audition CC)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name); Jim Wise; This is a 100% Flat transfer from the DAT no signal processing what-so-ever

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a fire‑filled Fillmore West night highlighted by the legendary Dark Star → St. Stephen sequence.
ai_review.review: The 16‑track SBD mix delivers exceptionally crisp separation—Jerry’s guitar swirls from fuzzy to ear‑piercing, Tom’s keys sit up front, and Bob’s rhythm work shines. Musically the show is a high‑energy classic: Dark Star rolls into St. Stephen with textbook intensity, complemented by standout moments on Mountains of the Moon, Good Morning, School Girl and Doin’ That Rag.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen five‑star reviews praise both the performance (exceptional Dark Star/St Stephen, high energy) and the recording (crisp, clear multitrack mix). The lone zero‑star review appears to be an outlier, so the combined weighted score is near perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: 16‑track SBD mix provides superb clarity and instrument separation; reviewers note crisp guitar, clear keyboards, and better fidelity than the Live/Dead vinyl/CD releases.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise three‑song first set followed by a second set built for the 16‑track recording; the band plays with deliberate focus and tight transitions that capture the historic Live/Dead material.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers rave about his tone—fuzzy to ear‑piercing, iconic "ta‑da‑DA" sequence in Dark Star, and overall presence.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass work is described as an impressive ‘maelstrom’, keeping the pulse throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm guitar is highlighted as clear and creative, especially on Dark Star and St. Stephen.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom (Keith)’s keyboards are noted as clearly audible and well‑balanced in the mix.
